Standard: The store and armament equipment withstand all design yield loads without yielding or detrimental deformation and can withstand design ultimate loads without rupture or collapsing failures for all operating environments in the flight envelope throughout the specified service life of the store. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct structural analysis to verify that the store structure can withstand all DLLs without yielding or detrimental deformation and can withstand design ultimate limit loads without failure. Loads and minimum margins of safety are compliant IAW MIL-STD-8591, Design Strength section and MIL-M-8856, Design Strength section. The analysis should describe the critical load cases and should account for relevant A, B, or S-basis and environmental knockdowns in material properties and allowables IAW MMPDS or CMH-17, as needed, for composite materials. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Determine store strength capability, to include store subassembly, component, and joining methods. Measure store deformation (strain) and deflection under all loads and substantiate pre-test analysis with lab test results.
  (2) Lab test: Conduct full-scale static test with test articles that are structurally representative of the store to ultimate load IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 130 and MIL-M-8856, Structural Demonstration Tests appendix and update strength analyses or supplement with additional lab tests as necessary. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (3) Flight test: Conduct loads test with structurally representative IMV to measure and validate design loads against flight conditions representative of the full flight envelope IAW MIL- HDBK-1763, Test 200. Compare measured flight test loads to strength analyses, lab test, and ground test and update analyses or re-accomplish lab or ground testing as necessary.
